Anna — great questions, thank you. High level answers up front, followed by details and an attached options matrix (redwood-data-retention-options.csv). Happy to walk through live.

Summary (top-line)
- Residency: For Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem), customer data remains in your VPC/region by default. Hosted metadata in the control plane can be configured to be region-restricted or customer-hosted.
- Deletion: We support tenant-scoped erasure. For hosted deployments we delete live data within 24-72 hours; backups and snapshots are on a separate retention cadence (see details below) but we can contractually reduce snapshot retention or provide an accelerated deletion SLA for enterprise agreements.
- Redaction: Multiple options — client-side redaction before call, server-side deterministic redaction pipelines (regex/token rules), reversible pseudonymization, and an optional Private plugin that runs customer-provided redactors pre-index. Choosing stronger redaction (e.g., client-side full tokenization) will reduce usable context for generation; pipeline redaction can keep structured features while removing PHI.

Detailed notes
1) Residency model
- Private (VPC): model weights and runtime operate inside customer network; logs and KV caches are only stored to customer-managed storage unless explicitly enabled to use Redwood-managed observability.
- Private (on-prem): all artifacts remain on-prem; Redwood can ship an audited installer and provide key rotation guidance.

2) Erasure and backups
- Live data deletion: tenant-level purge triggers remove indexes, KV caches, and request logs for the time window within 24–72 hours depending on size. We provide a deletion ticket and an automated job id that you can use to track progress.
- Backups & snapshotted state: standard policy retains incremental snapshots for 30 days. For Private deployments we can reduce or eliminate automatic snapshot retention via config or contract to enable immediate deletion of snapshot chains. For hosted + Dedicated customers: accelerated snapshot deletion can be requested; we will return a deletion certificate within the agreed SLA window (typically 7–30 days to account for immutable backup workflows).
- Model fine-tuning traces: Redwood does not fine-tune customer data into shared models by default. Any supervised fine-tuning or long-term derived artifacts require explicit opt-in and are covered by separate agreements; if present, those artifacts are purged on the same deletion schedule.

3) Redaction & minimization options
- Client-side pre-send redaction: you remove or tokenize PHI before it leaves customer systems (recommended for highest assurance).
- Server-side deterministic redaction: regex-based redactors, entity dictionaries, and policy rules applied in-order. Good balance between fidelity and safety.
- Pseudonymization/tokenization: reversible tokens stored in customer-managed KMS; useful for workflows that need re-identification under controlled conditions.
- Index-level hashing & salted digests: useful for deduplication without storing raw values.
- KV cache control: KV cache can be disabled or configured to not persist between restarts to minimize residual sensitive context.

Attachments: redwood-data-retention-options.csv (simple matrix: residency mode / backup behavior / expected deletion SLA)

Anna — answering the specifics you flagged and attaching a short playbook and disposal checklist for review (redaction-playbook-v1.pdf, data-disposal-steps.docx).

Backups & off-site copies
- Private VPC: by default backups are written to customer-managed buckets. Off-site archival only occurs if the customer enables Redwood-managed archival; otherwise there are no vendor-controlled off-site copies. We can include explicit contract language that prohibits Redwood-managed off-site archival for your account.
- Hosted/Dedicated: vendor-managed backups are part of our HA posture. We can offer a contractual accelerated deletion SLA and a backup-retention appendix that sets snapshot horizon to a lower bound (e.g., 7 days).

Deletion certificate contents (standard template)
- Tenant id / affected resources (index prefixes, KV namespaces)
- Deletion job id and start/end timestamps
- List of backup/snapshot ids removed (if applicable)
- Operator signature (automated system signature + Redwood compliance officer)
- Reference to supporting audit logs (export link or attached CSV)

Audit log export
- Yes — we provide exportable audit logs for deletion jobs and API calls. For Private deployments the logs live in your storage; for hosted we provide an export bundle on request (S3/CSV) that includes signed timestamps.

Recommended retention guidance (best practice)
- Short answer: minimize. For most PHI processing where ongoing access is not required, we recommend 90 days default with a contractual maximum (by default) of 7 years only when required by law or clinical needs.
- Examples: ephemeral inference (no long-term indexing) — 0–30 days; searchable index of clinical transcripts — 1–3 years typical, escalate to 7 years only if required.

Operational controls we recommend enabling for MediCore
- Disable KV caching for high-safety endpoints.
- Use client-side tokenization for direct identifiers and server-side pseudonymization for context used in analytics.
- Configure automatic retention policies per-index with explicit tombstone and snapshot purge windows.

I'll join the call and we'll bring the playbook and example certificate so procurement can validate.

—Naomi
